from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Planar graphs have no crossing edges.",
            "Vertices, edges, and faces define the structure.",
            "Faces include the unbounded outer region."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph", lecture_lines)

        # Graph setup
        square = Square(side_length=2, color=YELLOW)
        vertices = VGroup(*[Dot(point=p, color=WHITE) for p in square.get_vertices()])
        edges = VGroup(*[Line(square.get_vertices()[i], square.get_vertices()[(i+1)%4], color=YELLOW) for i in range(4)])
        graph = VGroup(vertices, edges)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        v_label = Text("V", color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        e_label = Text("E", color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "B2")
        v_label.next_to(vertices[0], UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(e_label, "C4")
        e_label.next_to(edges[0], RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(v_label), Write(e_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        
        face = Polygon(*square.get_vertices(), fill_opacity=0.3, color=RED)
        f_label = Text("F", color=RED).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(face, "C3", "D4")
        f_label.move_to(face.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(face), Write(f_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Euler's formula states V minus E plus F equals 2.",
            "This formula holds for any connected planar graph.",
            "V is vertices, E is edges, F is faces."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Euler’s Characteristic Formula", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize Formula
        formula = MathTex("V", "-", "E", "+", "F", "=", "2")
        formula.set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.add(formula)

        # Graph setup (Planar representation of a house)
        # Vertices: 5, Edges: 6, Faces: 3 (inc outer)
        nodes = [
            [-0.5, -0.5, 0], [0.5, -0.5, 0], 
            [-0.5, 0.5, 0], [0.5, 0.5, 0], [0, 1.0, 0]
        ]
        edges = [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3), (2, 4), (3, 4)]
        
        graph = VGroup()
        for edge in edges:
            line = Line(nodes[edge[0]], nodes[edge[1]], color=WHITE)
            graph.add(line)
        for node in nodes:
            dot = Dot(node, color=WHITE)
            graph.add(dot)
            
        self.place_in_area(graph, 'D4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(graph)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # Highlights based on B029
        v_part = formula.get_part_by_tex("V")
        e_part = formula.get_part_by_tex("E")
        f_part = formula.get_part_by_tex("F")
        
        self.play(v_part.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(e_part.animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(f_part.animate.set_color("#0000FF"))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Concept of the Dual Graph", [
            "Dual graphs place vertices inside each face.",
            "Edges connect vertices of adjacent faces.",
            "This creates a new linked structure."
        ])

        # Primal Graph (Triangle)
        # Vertices and Edges
        v1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v3 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        e1 = Line(v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e2 = Line(v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e3 = Line(v3.get_center(), v1.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        primal = VGroup(v1, v2, v3, e1, e2, e3)
        self.place_in_area(primal, "A4", "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Dual Vertices (Face centers)
        # For a simple triangle there are two faces: inner and outer.
        # But for clarity in this layout, we'll draw a graph with clear faces.
        # Let's redefine as a square with a diagonal for clear faces.
        
        v1, v2, v3, v4 = [Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(4)]
        self.place_at_grid(v1, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(v2, "B6")
        self.place_at_grid(v3, "D6")
        self.place_at_grid(v4, "D4")
        
        edges = VGroup(
            Line(v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(v3.get_center(), v4.get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(v4.get_center(), v1.get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(v1.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        )
        primal = VGroup(v1, v2, v3, v4, edges)
        self.add(primal)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Dual vertices
        f1_center = np.array([2.3, 0.4, 0]) # Center of top-right triangle
        f2_center = np.array([3.1, -0.4, 0]) # Center of bottom-left triangle
        
        d1 = Dot(color="#FFFF00")
        d2 = Dot(color="#FFFF00")
        d1.move_to(f1_center)
        d2.move_to(f2_center)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(d1), FadeIn(d2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        dual_edge = Line(d1.get_center(), d2.get_center(), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(dual_edge))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            primal.animate.set_opacity(0.2),
            FadeIn(VGroup(d1, d2, dual_edge)) # Highlight
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Deep Dive: The Duality Relationship", [
            "Duality preserves edges but swaps vertices and faces.",
            "V star equals F, F star equals V.",
            "E star equals E holds perfectly."
        ])
        
        # Setup visualization objects
        # Using simple shapes to represent graph duality concepts
        v_prime = MathTex("V^* = F", color="#FF00FF")
        f_prime = MathTex("F^* = V", color="#FF00FF")
        e_prime = MathTex("E^* = E", color="#00FFFF")
        
        dual_group = VGroup(v_prime, f_prime, e_prime).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Duality preserves edges but swaps vertices and faces.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_in_area(dual_group, "B4", "E6", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(dual_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # V star equals F, F star equals V.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.play(Indicate(v_prime), Indicate(f_prime))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # E star equals E holds perfectly.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Indicate(e_prime))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Duality simplifies complex network problems.",
                         "It aids circuit design and map coloring.",
                         "Use duality for efficient routing pathways."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Application", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1: Euler's formula V - E + F = 2 ===
        formula = MathTex("V - E + F = 2", font_size=42, color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A1", "B6")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2: Duality relationship V' = F, E' = E ===
        dual_text = MathTex("V' = F, \\quad E' = E", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(dual_text, "C1", "D6")
        self.play(FadeIn(dual_text))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3: Map application ===
        map_region = Square(side_length=1.5, color=GREEN).rotate(PI/4)
        map_label = Text("Map Partition", font_size=24, color=WHITE).next_to(map_region, DOWN)
        group = VGroup(map_region, map_label)
        self.place_in_area(group, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(map_region), Write(map_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Unlocking Planar Graph Duality and Euler's Characteristic Formula
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Discrete Mathematics)

sections.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
sections.content: Define a planar graph as a graph that can be drawn in a 2D plane without edges crossing. Introduce the concepts of Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F), where a 'Face' is an enclosed region, including the outer unbounded region.
sections.example: Visualizing a simple square: 4 vertices, 4 edges, and 2 faces (the inside and the outside).

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
sections.content: Introduce Euler's formula: V - E + F = 2. Explain that this holds true for any connected planar graph, forming a fundamental invariant of the surface geometry.
sections.example: Animate a triangle (V=3, E=3, F=2 -> 3-3+2=2) morphing into a house-shaped graph (V=5, E=6, F=3 -> 5-6+3=2) to show the constant result.

sections.title: Concept of the Dual Graph
sections.content: Explain the construction of a Dual Graph (G*): Place a new vertex in every face of the original graph. Connect two new vertices if their corresponding faces share an edge in the original graph.
sections.example: Imagine a honeybee hive pattern (hexagonal grid); the dual graph links the centers of adjacent hexagons to form a triangular lattice.

sections.title: Deep Dive: The Duality Relationship
sections.content: Highlight the mathematical relationship between the original graph and its dual: V* = F, F* = V, and E* = E. Demonstrate how this transformation maps the complexity of one graph onto the structure of another.
sections.example: Take a 3D Polyhedron, like a cube, projected as a 2D planar graph. The dual graph corresponds to its geometric dual—the octahedron.

sections.title: Summary and Application
sections.content: Wrap up by explaining that duality is not just a theoretical tool but a method for simplifying circuit design, map coloring problems, and network routing in planar topologies.
sections.example: Show a complex circuit board layout (graph) and explain how engineers use the dual graph to find efficient pathways for signal routing.
